Averaged vs BLUE phenotypes — how trait construction changes BLINK¶

Setup. Same genotypes (98,026 SNPs), same model (GAPIT/BLINK), same settings. The only difference is the trait value fed to GWAS:

  • averaged — naive environment-average of a genotype's plot records (confounded with which environments it was grown in);
  • BLUE — environment/rep/block-adjusted estimate from a fixed-effects model (the de-confounding fix).

Question. Does swapping the phenotype change (1) calibration/inflation, (2) the number of hits, and (3) which loci BLINK nominates? These are separable:

Diagnostic If trait construction is minor If BLINK is phenotype-sensitive
λ_GC, QQ, bulk fraction similar between runs (may still look similar — BLINK self-calibrates)
# significant hits similar similar or shifted
per-SNP p-value agreement & shared hits high low (different loci)

Data: averaged BLINK = gapit/results/; BLUE BLINK = local_experiments/results_blue/; all 16 trait×stress combinations, merged on SNP ID. (Locus overlap within LD windows is covered separately in 03_ld_decay; here we compare the runs' statistical character and per-SNP agreement.)

import warnings, glob
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
%matplotlib inline
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "savefig.dpi": 200, "font.size": 10,
                     "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": 0.25})

PROJECT = Path("/path/to/PLANT_PROJECT")
AVG  = PROJECT/"gapit"/"results"                    # averaged-trait BLINK
BLUE = PROJECT/"local_experiments"/"results_blue"   # BLUE-trait BLINK
FIGDIR = PROJECT/"local_experiments"/"figures"; FIGDIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

TRAITS = ["yield","anthesis","silking","ASI"]
STRESS = ["NO_STRESS","HEAT_STRESSED","DROUGHT_STRESSED","HEAT_DROUGHT_STRESSED"]
CONDS  = [f"{t}_{s}" for t in TRAITS for s in STRESS]
NSNP   = 98026; BONF = 0.05/NSNP
CHI2_MED = stats.chi2.ppf(0.5, 1)
print("conditions:", len(CONDS), "| Bonferroni p <", f"{BONF:.2e}")

conditions: 16 | Bonferroni p < 5.10e-07
In [2]:
def lambda_gc(p):
    p = np.asarray(p, float); p = p[(p > 0) & (p <= 1)]
    return np.median(stats.chi2.isf(p, 1)) / CHI2_MED

def bulk_fracs(p):
    p = np.asarray(p, float); p = p[(p > 0) & (p <= 1)]
    return {"p<=0.5": (p<=0.5).mean(), "p<=0.1": (p<=0.1).mean(),
            "p<=0.05": (p<=0.05).mean(), "p<=0.01": (p<=0.01).mean()}

def qq_xy(p):
    p = np.sort(np.asarray(p, float)); p = p[(p > 0) & (p <= 1)]; n = len(p)
    return -np.log10((np.arange(1, n+1)-0.5)/n), -np.log10(p)

def load_blink(base, cond):
    g = [x for x in glob.glob(str(Path(base)/f"{cond}_BLINK"/"GAPIT.Association.GWAS_Results.BLINK.*.csv"))
         if "(NYC)" not in x]
    if not g: return None
    df = pd.read_csv(g[0], usecols=["SNP","Chr","Pos","P.value"])
    df["P.value"] = pd.to_numeric(df["P.value"], errors="coerce")
    return df.dropna(subset=["SNP","P.value"])

print("helpers ready")

helpers ready

2. Calibration — λ_GC, QQ, bulk¶

Are the two runs differently inflated? λ_GC = median(χ²)/0.4549 (≈1 = calibrated). BLINK absorbs polygenic background into pseudo-QTN covariates, so both runs are expected to be near-calibrated — the point is to confirm the phenotype swap doesn't break that, so any later differences are about which loci, not inflation.

In [4]:

                    for c in CONDS}).T

Read-out. Both runs are similarly calibrated (λ_GC near 1, QQ near the diagonal, bulk fractions near null) — BLINK self-calibrates regardless of the phenotype. So any difference between the runs is not about inflation; it's about which loci they pick. That's §3.

3. Do they find the same loci? — per-SNP agreement & shared hits¶

Merge the two runs on SNP. Spearman of −log₁₀(p) measures whether the genome-wide signal ranks agree; shared Bonferroni hits measures top-hit overlap. High = the phenotype swap barely matters; low = BLINK nominates different loci depending on how the trait was built.

In [7]:
rows = []; scatter = []
for c in CONDS:
    if c not in A or c not in B: continue
    mg = A[c][["SNP","P.value"]].merge(B[c][["SNP","P.value"]], on="SNP", suffixes=("_avg","_blue"))
    if mg.empty: continue
    rho = stats.spearmanr(-np.log10(mg["P.value_avg"]), -np.log10(mg["P.value_blue"])).correlation
    sa, sb = mg["P.value_avg"]<BONF, mg["P.value_blue"]<BONF
    rows.append({"condition":c, "avg_sig":int(sa.sum()), "blue_sig":int(sb.sum()),
                 "shared_sig":int((sa & sb).sum()), "spearman_-log10p":round(rho,3)})
    scatter.append((c, mg))
agree = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("condition")
display(agree)
T = agree.sum(numeric_only=True)
print(f"\nTOTAL: averaged {int(T.avg_sig)} hits, BLUE {int(T.blue_sig)} hits, shared {int(T.shared_sig)} "
      f"({100*T.shared_sig/max(T.blue_sig,1):.1f}% of BLUE)")
print(f"median per-SNP -log10p Spearman across conditions: {agree['spearman_-log10p'].median():.3f}")

n = len(scatter); ncol = 4; nrow = int(np.ceil(n/ncol))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrow, ncol, figsize=(15, 3.4*nrow), squeeze=False)
for ax,(c,mg) in zip(axes.ravel(), scatter):
    x = -np.log10(mg["P.value_avg"]); y = -np.log10(mg["P.value_blue"])
    ax.scatter(x, y, s=3, alpha=0.2, color="#7f8c8d", rasterized=True)
    bl = -np.log10(BONF); ax.axhline(bl, color="#2980b9", ls=":", lw=0.8); ax.axvline(bl, color="#c0392b", ls=":", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_title(c, fontsize=8); ax.set_xlabel("avg -log10p", fontsize=8); ax.set_ylabel("BLUE -log10p", fontsize=8)
for ax in axes.ravel()[n:]: ax.axis("off")
fig.suptitle("Per-SNP signal agreement: averaged vs BLUE BLINK (dotted = Bonferroni)", y=1.0, fontsize=12)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(FIGDIR/"avgblue_concordance.png", bbox_inches="tight"); plt.show()

4. Summary¶

  • Calibration is unchanged by the phenotype swap — both averaged and BLUE BLINK are near-calibrated (λ_GC ≈ 1, clean QQ, near-null bulk).
  • Hit counts are comparable between the two runs.
  • But the loci barely overlap — per-SNP −log₁₀(p) ranks are nearly uncorrelated and shared Bonferroni hits are few. A justified change in trait construction (which only moderately changes the phenotype values) reshuffles essentially all of BLINK's nominated loci.

Implication. BLINK's locus selection is highly sensitive to phenotype construction in this panel; the trait-building choice must be fixed and justified before its loci are treated as findings. (Positional locus overlap within the LD-derived ±16/±32 kb windows is quantified in 03_ld_decay.)
